summary: What worked: halving TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 while keeping DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=128 so grad_accum stays 1 (-0.0088, my run 364f25b 0.988497), and then widening the model at that batch. I mapped the width ladder at depth 8 / batch 2**18 / DB=128 to its optimum: 512 -> 0.9885, 640 -> 0.9847, 768 -> 0.9818 (peer commit 6dd0342), 896 -> 0.9934 (my 6e53f33). Depth is the wrong axis once the model is wide: dim 640 x depth 10 gave 0.986247, worse than dim 640 x depth 8. What did not work: U-net style learnable skip connections (0.989854 vs 0.988497 - the existing resid_lambdas/x0_lambdas already cover it), all-L attention windows at the best shape (0.983388 vs 0.981817 for SSSL), and value embeddings on all 8 layers instead of alternating (0.982139, a tie with 0.981817 for +25M params and 3% slower steps). I also aborted a queued 2**17 run before it claimed the GPU after results.tsv showed every DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=64 run sitting ~0.010 worse regardless of total batch. What I would try next: the shape and schedule surface is flat around dim 768 / depth 8 / SSSL / 2**18, so the remaining headroom is in per-step cost rather than hyperparameters - chunked or fused cross-entropy to kill the fp32 logits tensor (8.6GB per microbatch at B*T=262144 x 8192 vocab) would buy 10-20% more optimizer steps at identical quality, which on this curve is worth about 0.003 bpb, and that is the one change I would spend the next run on.
